title: South St. Paul High enrolls 217 10th-graders for 2024-25 reading MCA
text:
South St. Paul High enrolls 217 10th-graders for 2024-25 reading MCA
According to the Minnesota Department of Education, South St. Paul High School had only 10th-graders complete the reading section of the 2024-25 MCA.
Of the students assessed during this cycle at South St. Paul High School, all 217 belonged to the 10th grade.
This figure marks an increase from the prior school year, which saw 207 10th-graders take the reading MCA assessment.
About 39% of these 10th-graders met reading proficiency by test benchmarks.
The MCA and the Alternate Minnesota Comprehensive Assessment (Alt MCA) serve as Minnesota’s primary state exams measuring academic progress and fulfilling both federal and state requirements. Depending on grade level, students are tested in math, reading, and science. Most participate in the MCA, while some receiving special education services who qualify may take the Alt MCA.
Statewide MCA proficiency rates in Minnesota have decreased since before the pandemic, based on information from the state's Report Card. Math proficiency dropped more than 7% since 2019, and reading was down nearly 5%.
This information comes from the Minnesota Department of Education. Source data is available here.
